claim_type_rationale: The universe rule is deterministic and source-defined by closed canonical IAVCEI designation: Wikipedia's `Decade Volcanoes` master article enumerates the 16 volcanoes selected by the International Association of Volcanology and Chemistry of the Earth's Interior under the UN International Decade for Natural Disaster Reduction (1990s). The list has been stable since the original designations in 1991. Universe membership = 'listed in IAVCEI Decade Volcanoes program per Wikipedia Decade Volcanoes article' — no curator judgment. Per-row cell values (Country, Highest Elevation Meters, Last Known Eruption Start Year) are taken from the master article's consolidated table. Sovereign-State Continent is curator-mapped from Country per the locked normalization rule (which itself is source-grounded: continent of sovereign country for overseas-island cases; listed volcano region's continent for transcontinental sovereign states). Mirror precedent for closed-canonical-list source_defined: `twelve_olympians_greek_to_roman` (13 rows, closed canonical Greek-deity list).

Single PK Volcano.

decision_log.rationale: The IAVCEI Decade Volcanoes is a closed 16-entry list maintained since 1991. Wikipedia 'Decade Volcanoes' article enumerates the 16 with stable membership. No curator judgment for universe membership; deterministic universe rule. Distinct from candidate_rebuild (no curator-bounded universe selection) and from partially_supplemented (no rebuilding of the master subset). Mirror precedent: `twelve_olympians_greek_to_roman` (closed canonical Greek-deity list of 13).

decision_log.decision: Universe source = master Decade_Volcanoes Wikipedia article only; per-volcano articles validation-only
decision_log.rationale: Per audit cycle-2 finding: 'source_count = 1 is acceptable because the master table supplies universe membership plus Country/Elevation/Last-known-eruption values; per-volcano pages can stay as validation prose.' The master article's consolidated table is sufficient for all 5 staged cell types. Per-volcano Wikipedia articles add no new universe or value-role anchors; they cross-check the master table's values.

decision_log.decision: Avachinsky-Koryaksky = 1 row (not 2); Highest Elevation Meters = 3456 (Koryaksky); Last Known Eruption Start Year = 2009 (later of paired)
decision_log.rationale: Per audit cycle-1 BLOCKING fix #1 + cycle-2 confirmation: IAVCEI lists 'Avachinsky-Koryaksky' as a paired Decade Volcano (twin volcanoes near Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky, Russia, treated as a single entry). Wikipedia 'Decade Volcanoes' article treats as one entry. Scalar reduction rules: Highest Elevation Meters uses Koryaksky's 3456m (higher of Avachinsky 2741 / Koryaksky 3456); Last Known Eruption Start Year uses 2009 (later of Avachinsky 2008 / Koryaksky 2009). This preserves the 16-entry IAVCEI universe.

decision_log.decision: Santa María = 1 row (not separately Santiaguito); volcano name per Wikipedia 'Santa María (volcano)' canonical title; Last Known Eruption Start Year follows master table verbatim
decision_log.rationale: Santa María (Guatemala, 3772m) was designated the Decade Volcano. Its post-1902-eruption lava dome complex Santiaguito (also Guatemala, lower elevation ~2520m) is part of the same volcanic system but is a separate edifice. Wikipedia's 'Decade Volcanoes' article lists 'Santa María / Santiaguito' as a single combined entry. Per Wikipedia's per-volcano article canonical title, the staged volcano name is 'Santa María'. Santiaguito documented as a related-system dome in this decision_log entry but not a separate row. Last Known Eruption Start Year for Santa María staged as 2013 — the master article's `Last known eruption` cell for Santa María shows `23 August 2013`, extracted to integer start year 2013 per the locked extraction rule. The cycle-0 staging committed an incorrect 1902 value (rationalized around the historical Plinian eruption that established the Santiaguito dome complex); this was caught by cycle-1 post-staging audit BLOCKING finding and corrected in cycle-2 to follow the master table verbatim per the source_count=1 source plan. The historical 1902 Plinian eruption and Santiaguito's continuous dome activity from 1922-present are background context but NOT the cell value — the cell value is whatever the master article's `Last known eruption` column shows.

decision_log.decision: Last Known Eruption Start Year (renamed from 'Most Recent Known Eruption Year' per audit cycle-2 staging-edit #1)
decision_log.rationale: Per audit cycle-2 staging-edit #1: the master article shows 'YEAR-present' for ongoing eruptions (e.g., Etna '2013–present', Nyiragongo '22 May 2021–present'); extracting the year yields the start year of the listed ongoing eruption, NOT literally the most recent eruption year. The column name was renamed to honestly reflect the semantics. Extraction rule: for date-with-day-precision values (e.g., Sakurajima '16 November 2025') → extract integer year 2025; for year-with-status values (e.g., Etna '2013–present') → extract integer start year 2013; for paired-volcano entries → use later of paired start years. Replaces the cycle-1 design's VEI≥2 threshold (which was rejected by audit cycle-1 BLOCKING fix #2 as not source-stable).

decision_log.decision: Sovereign-State Continent column (renamed from 'Continent' per audit cycle-1 HYGIENE fix; with transcontinental edge-case rule per audit cycle-2 staging-edit #2)
decision_log.rationale: Per audit cycle-1 HYGIENE: 'Continent' was ambiguous for overseas-island cases (Teide on Canary Islands, Mauna Loa in Hawaii). Cycle-1 fix: rename to 'Sovereign-State Continent' with normalization rule 'continent of the sovereign country in which the volcano is located, NOT physical island geography'. Cycle-2 staging-edit #2: tighten with transcontinental edge-case wording 'Use the sovereign-state political continent for overseas island cases; for transcontinental sovereign states, use the listed volcano region's continent'. This handles: Teide (Canary Islands → Spain → Europe, overseas-island case → Europe per sovereignty); Mauna Loa (Hawaii → United States → North America, overseas-island case → North America per US sovereignty); Avachinsky-Koryaksky (Kamchatka → Russia, transcontinental-state edge case → Asia per Kamchatka being Asian Russia).

decision_log.decision: Category = geographic primary; secondary = set_filter (per audit cycle-2 confirmation; NOT hierarchical_decomposition)
decision_log.rationale: Per audit cycle-1 + cycle-2: 'geographic primary is defensible; set_filter secondary is also appropriate. I would not use hierarchical_decomposition.' Decade Volcanoes differ from top-N-per-continent patterns (which would be hierarchical_decomposition) because per-continent row counts are determined by IAVCEI selection, NOT by curator-selected top-N. Geographic primary captures the 'curated set with geographic distribution' shape; set_filter secondary captures the 'universe-membership filter on the global volcano set' shape. operation_type = filter (universe selection by IAVCEI-list membership).

decision_log.decision: Entity class = physical-features/volcanoes (NEW fine-class extending physical-features bucket from 7 to 8 instances)
decision_log.rationale: Per picker entity-class taxonomy: physical-features bucket currently has 7 fine-classes (mountains, rivers ×2, deserts, islands, oceanic-trenches, lakes). 'volcanoes' is a NEW fine-class within this established bucket. The PK Volcano is an individual physical entity (a specific volcanic edifice or paired-edifice system), matching the physical-features bucket convention (individual mountains, individual rivers, etc.). Answer-entity-wins rule: Volcano is the answer entity; Sovereign-State Continent is the partition scaffold.

normalization_decisions.rule: Volcano name per the master 'Decade Volcanoes' article's row label, matching the per-volcano Wikipedia article canonical title where the master gives a short form. Avachinsky-Koryaksky as a single hyphenated entry per IAVCEI canonical labeling (paired-volcano twin entry). Santa María (not 'Santa Maria / Santiaguito') per the per-volcano article canonical title. Mount Etna / Mount Vesuvius / Mount Rainier with 'Mount' prefix per Wikipedia article titles. Volcán de Colima (Spanish title) preserved per Wikipedia 'Volcán de Colima' article.

Continent of the sovereign country in which the volcano is located, per the master article's Country column. Normalization rule (locked at cycle-2 staging-edit #2): 'Use the sovereign-state political continent for overseas island cases; for transcontinental sovereign states, use the listed volcano region's continent.' Applies as follows: (a) overseas-island cases: Teide (Canary Islands → Spain → Europe per sovereignty); Mauna Loa (Hawaii → United States → North America per sovereignty); (b) transcontinental-state edge case: Avachinsky-Koryaksky (Kamchatka → Russia, transcontinental → Asia per Kamchatka being Asian Russia, not the Russia-as-European default). Closed 6-value vocabulary: Africa / Asia / Europe / North America / Oceania / South America. No 'Antarctica' value because no Decade Volcanoes are in Antarctica.

Sovereign country name per the master article's Country column. Verbatim: 'Democratic Republic of the Congo' (full form per Wikipedia convention, NOT 'DR Congo' or 'DRC'); 'United States' (NOT 'USA' or 'U.S.'); 'Papua New Guinea'; 'Italy', 'Spain', 'Greece', 'Mexico', 'Japan', 'Indonesia', 'Russia', 'Philippines', 'Colombia', 'Guatemala'.

Integer meters above sea level per the master article's Elevation column. For paired-volcano entries (Avachinsky-Koryaksky), use the higher of the paired elevations (Koryaksky 3456m, higher than Avachinsky 2741m). All values per master article; per-volcano Wikipedia article infoboxes consulted as validation cross-checks (the periodic_table_groups precedent applies here).

Integer year extracted from the master article's 'Last known eruption' column per cycle-2 staging-edit #1 column rename. Extraction conventions: (a) for plain-year values (e.g., '1944') → use as-is; (b) for date-with-day-precision values (e.g., '16 November 2025' for Sakurajima) → extract integer year 2025; (c) for year-with-status values where the eruption is ongoing (e.g., '2013–present' for Etna; '22 May 2021–present' for Nyiragongo) → extract integer START year of the listed ongoing eruption (2013, 2021 respectively); (d) for paired-volcano entries (Avachinsky 2008 / Koryaksky 2009) → use later of paired start years (2009). The column name 'Last Known Eruption Start Year' was chosen at cycle-2 (renamed from 'Most Recent Known Eruption Year') to honestly reflect that for ongoing eruptions, the extracted integer is the START year of the listed eruption, NOT literally the most recent eruption year. For Santa María, the master article's `Last known eruption` cell shows `23 August 2013`, extracted to integer start year 2013 per the locked extraction rule — NOT the 1902 Plinian eruption that established the Santiaguito dome complex (the 1902 cycle-0 staging value was corrected in cycle-2 hygiene repair to follow the master table verbatim per source_count=1 plan). Santiaguito's continuous dome activity from 1922-present is background context but NOT the cell value.

open_questions.question: Should the Sovereign-State Continent column use the 6-continent or 7-continent model (i.e., should North America and South America be combined into 'Americas')?
open_questions.answer: 6-continent model with North America and South America as separate values, per the master article's per-volcano regional placement (Galeras in South America; Colima/Rainier/Santa María/Mauna Loa in North America). The 6-continent model also matches the precedent set by `top_5_highest_mountains_per_continent` (uses Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, Oceania, South America).

open_questions.question: If a new volcano is added to the IAVCEI Decade Volcanoes list after the original 16, should the instance expand?
open_questions.answer: Universe is locked to the master Wikipedia 'Decade Volcanoes' article as of 2026-05-17. If Wikipedia later adds entries, a follow-up cycle would re-stage. The IAVCEI program is historically associated with the 1990s UN International Decade for Natural Disaster Reduction; new designations are rare. temporal_sensitivity = low reflects this stability.

open_questions.question: How is Santiaguito treated separately from Santa María?
open_questions.answer: Santiaguito is the post-1902 lava dome complex of the Santa María volcanic system, with continuous dome activity from 1922-present. Per the master article and per-volcano canonical title, the staged row is 'Santa María' with elevation 3772m (Santa María's summit). Santiaguito (~2520m) is NOT a separate row. The Last Known Eruption Start Year cell value for Santa María is 2013 (extracted from the master article's `23 August 2013` cell per the locked extraction rule). The earlier 1902 Plinian eruption and Santiaguito's post-1922 continuous activity are background context but NOT the cell value. (Cycle-0 staging committed an incorrect 1902 value; corrected to 2013 in cycle-2 hygiene repair per cycle-1 audit BLOCKING finding.)
